item.title: PM stresses discipline, professionalism, public trust in armed forces
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday urged members of the armed forces to remain committed to the Constitution, laws, military regulations and humanitarian values while discharging their duties, saying discipline, professionalism and public trust are fundamental to the strength of the forces.
While speaking at a ceremony to present National Standard to several battalions and regiments of the Bangladesh Army at Savar Cantonment, he also stressed the need to modernise the armed forces, strengthen domestic defence production and develop new technological capabilities to meet changing security challenges.
“An armed force’s strength is not limited to weapons, equipment or manpower. Its real strength lies in discipline, skills, leadership, morality, training and public trust,” the prime minister said, stressing the importance of maintaining the chain of command.
He said modern warfare increasingly involves cyberspace, outer space, drones, artificial intelligence, electronic warfare and information-based capabilities, making it necessary for Bangladesh to keep its defence preparedness in line with changing global security conditions.
Congratulating the units that received the National Standard, Tarique Rahman said the honour represents their history, tradition, discipline, sacrifice, professionalism and commitment to the country.
He said receiving the National Standard is a renewed pledge to perform their duties with greater dedication, while protecting the honour of the national flag remains a sacred responsibility for every soldier.
The prime minister said the government is continuing efforts to make the armed forces more technology-driven, skilled, disciplined, professional and modern.
He said the government is also giving importance to establishing a domestic defence industry to produce necessary weapons, ammunition and other defence equipment in the country.
However, technology could never replace people, Tarique Rahman said, adding that Bangladesh needs an integrated defence capability in which the Army, Navy and Air Force can work together effectively when required.
He said the government is giving importance to the welfare of military personnel, including housing, healthcare, education, training, career development and social security after retirement.
The prime minister said salaries and allowances for members of the armed forces have already been increased by between 100 and 138% under the National Pay Scale.
The implementation of the “One Rank, One Pension” system is also in process to improve the living standards of military personnel, he added.
Tarique Rahman said protecting national interests, sovereignty and dignity will remain a key commitment for Bangladesh in the future.
He said Bangladesh wants to strengthen friendship and cooperation with all countries on the basis of mutual respect and equality.
Recalling the history of the Bangladesh Army, the Prime Minister said the birth of the force was closely linked to the country's independence and the 1971 War of Liberation.
He referred to the role of Major Ziaur Rahman, then deputy commander of the Eighth East Bengal Regiment, in Chattogram after the Pakistani military launched its crackdown on freedom-seeking people on the night of March 25, 1971.
Quoting Ziaur Rahman's account in his article The Birth of a Nation, Tarique Rahman said he had gathered Bengali-speaking officers and soldiers of the regiment and ordered them to take part in the armed struggle for independence at 2:15am on March 26.
He also recalled Ziaur Rahman's subsequent declaration of independence from Kalurghat Radio Centre on March 27, saying his role in the War of Liberation remained an inspiring chapter for the armed forces.
The prime minister said people who love their country and independence regard the success of the Army as a success for Bangladesh.
He said the armed forces play an important role not only in national defence but also in responding to disasters, floods, cyclones, fires and other national emergencies.
They are also earning a good reputation through peacekeeping missions abroad, Tarique Rahman said.
The ceremony was organised by the 9th Infantry Division of the Bangladesh Army. Ministers, advisers, the Army chief, members of the diplomatic corps, former and serving military officers, junior commissioned officers and other members of the armed forces attended the event.

item.title: Canada reports deaths after 'incident' on military base
item.description:
Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said late Saturday there were "fatalities and injuries" following an incident at a military base in western Canada.
"I'm saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base," identified as Wainwright in Alberta, McGuinty said.
Prime Minister Mark Carney had posted to X earlier Saturday that "a serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred at the base.
Neither offered details on the number of casualties or the nature of the incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, located about 200 kilometres (110 miles) southeast of Edmonton.
"We will have more to say in the coming hours and days," McGuinty said.

item.title: Grameen Kalyan appeals HC verdict on Tk666 crore tax
item.description:
An appeal has been filed against a High Court verdict directing Grameen Kalyan, an organisation owned by former interim government chief adviser Dr Muhammad Yunus, to pay Tk666 crore in taxes demanded by the National Board of Revenue (NBR).
The appeal was filed on behalf of Grameen Kalyan with the relevant section of the Appellate Division on Sunday.
On September 10, the High Court ruled that Grameen Kalyan must pay the Tk666 crore claimed by the NBR. The verdict was delivered by a bench comprising Justice Md Mujibur Rahman Miah and Justice Rezaul Karim after dismissing a rule issued in response to a writ petition.
Barristers Abdullah Al Mamun and Fida M Kamal represented Yunus in court.
The full text of the verdict was released on October 12 after being signed by the presiding judges. The documents comprised 15 and 32 pages.
On October 4, 2024, following the July mass uprising, a High Court bench comprising Justice Mohammad Khurshid Alam Sarkar and Justice Sardar Md Rashed Jahangir suo motu withdrew the verdict directing Grameen Kalyan to pay the Tk666 crore claimed by the NBR. The case files were also sent to the chief justice.
The matter was subsequently referred to a new bench for a hearing.
The dispute stems from two writ petitions filed by Grameen Kalyan in 2017 challenging tax demands following reassessments for the 2012-13, 2013-14, 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17 fiscal years. The court initially issued a rule after hearing the petitions, but a newly constituted High Court bench later dismissed it and delivered the verdict.
With the writ petitions dismissed, the NBR can proceed to collect the outstanding income tax from Grameen Kalyan, lawyers said.

item.title: Editors’ Council condemns murder of journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir
item.description:
The Editors’ Council has strongly condemned the murder of journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir, describing it as a grave attack on independent journalism, freedom of expression and the public’s right to know.
In a statement issued on Sunday, the council said ensuring journalists’ safety was a fundamental responsibility of a democratic state and that the culture of impunity surrounding attacks on and the murder of journalists was unacceptable.
The council expressed deep sympathy for Fakir’s bereaved family and solidarity with his colleagues.
It demanded a fair, impartial, transparent and swift investigation into the murder, calling for the immediate arrest and exemplary punishment of everyone involved, directly or indirectly.
The investigation must also examine whether the killing was linked to political, personal or professional disputes and whether Fakir had received any threats before his death, the statement said.
It added that everyone involved must be brought to justice, regardless of their political affiliation, social status or influence.
Any obstruction of the legal process, whether through pressure from influential quarters or attempts by suspects to evade arrest, would undermine journalists’ safety and public confidence in the rule of law, the council said.
The council called on the government and law enforcement agencies to take immediate and effective measures to ensure journalists’ safety.
It also urged democratic forces, civil society and other stakeholders to unite in defending press freedom and protecting journalists, stressing that intimidation, attacks and murder must not be allowed to silence the pursuit of truth.
The council said those responsible for Fakir’s murder must face exemplary punishment and that the culture of impunity surrounding attacks on journalists must end.
Lutforzzaman Alif Fakir, Netrokona correspondent for the private internet protocol television (IPTV) channel Ruposhi Bangla, was shot dead in the Telanjia area of Durgapur on the night of October 15, according to media reports.

item.title: Case filed against Tup-Tup Resort owner, manager arrested
item.description:
A case has been filed with Ukhia police over a fire at Tup-Tup Resort on Marine Drive in Cox’s Bazar that killed 10 tourists. The resort’s owner, Tanvir, and manager, Suman, have been named as accused.
A sub-inspector of Ukhia police filed the case on Saturday night, Officer-in-Charge Atiqur Rahman Majumder confirmed.
He said Suman, who was detained on Saturday afternoon, had been formally arrested in connection with the case.
Suman will be produced before a court on Sunday, while police are conducting operations to arrest the other accused, the OC said.
Meanwhile, a five-member investigation committee formed by the district administration is investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.
The fire broke out at Tup-Tup Resort and Restaurant on Saturday morning. Fire Service personnel recovered 10 bodies from the scene. DNA testing will be conducted to identify the victims, Majumder said.
He said the bodies would be handed over to the respective families after their identities were confirmed through DNA tests. The tests are intended to resolve discrepancies involving the recovered bodies, missing persons and the identification process.
The bodies will remain at the morgue of Cox’s Bazar District Sadar Hospital until the process is completed.
Abul Kalam Azad, special superintendent of police at the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) in Cox’s Bazar, said arrangements would be made to collect samples for DNA testing.
He said collection points will be set up at hospitals across Cox’s Bazar, adding that a team of CID experts from Dhaka could be brought in if necessary to facilitate the process locally.
Meanwhile, resort owner Tanvir has remained untraceable since the fire.

item.title: Why columns matter
Revenge is not a development strategy
There can be no development without employment
item.description:
The latest findings from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), revealing that nearly 29% of highly educated youth in Bangladesh are unemployed, while half of those employed work in jobs far below their qualifications, tells us that when it comes to job creation and employment, we are, without question, a profound socio-economic failure.
For a nation that has been banking on its demographic dividend to propel it into future prosperity for some time now, these numbers are not only depressing, but simultaneously a damning indictment of our archaic educational framework and haphazard labour market.
When nearly a third of our brightest minds are left idle or underemployed, it is certainly not just a statistical concern but a squandering of national potential. It is the type of squandering that threatens long-term economic stagnation for this country.
The root of this crisis is a glaring, persistent mismatch between what our academic institutions teach and what the modern economy actually demands. For decades, traditional degrees have churned out graduates disconnected from industrial reality, while technical, vocational, and digital skills training remain woefully neglected.
Compounding this, our labour markets remain choked by an overwhelming informal sector that lacks job security, formal contracts, and career progression, while bureaucracy, favouritism, and connections keep out worthy candidates from ever taking on roles fit for their qualifications.
Treating youth unemployment as a temporary inconvenience or relying on fragmented, cosmetic training programs will no longer suffice. Turning our demographic growth into a genuine economic advantage requires immediate, aggressive structural overhaul.
For that to happen, the state, in partnership with private industry, must radically modernize our curricula to align with market demands, prioritizing technical competency, critical thinking, and digital fluency. Public investment must also prioritize creating high-productivity jobs while providing robust support for innovative enterprises.
We cannot preach national development while forcing our graduates into despair and underemployment. Without equipping our youth with meaningful, dignified employment, there can be no development.

item.title: Sympathy alone will not extinguish flames
item.description:
Our hearts go out to the grieving families of the victims who lost their lives in the horrifying fire at the Tup-Tup Resort in Cox’s Bazar. That unsuspecting vacationers seeking peace in our country’s most popular tourist district should instead be trapped in an inferno is a heartbreaking tragedy.
Yet, beyond offering sympathy, we must confront, once again, the criminal negligence and systemic failure that allow these death traps to operate with impunity.
The revelation that, as per the fire service department, the resort lacked a valid fire safety license -- and had explicitly ignored official warnings issued in June -- transforms this tragedy from an accident into a predictable, preventable crime.
Constructing a multi-storey commercial establishment out of highly combustible bamboo and wood without mandatory suppression infrastructure, emergency exits, or staff training is a direct gamble with human lives. That resort personnel reportedly fled the scene as the flames spread only highlights a complete breakdown of duty of care.
This tragedy exposes a chronic failure of regulatory enforcement which is not limited to just factories and warehouses. Official warnings and post-disaster probes are utterly meaningless if authorities allow unlicensed, unsafe establishments to continue.
It goes without saying that a full investigation is necessary. Moreover, we need a sweeping, unyielding audit of every hotel, resort, and commercial venue in tourist zones that must be carried out without delay.
Unlicensed and non-compliant properties must be shut down, and the owners and regulators who ignored explicit safety warnings must face prosecution to the fullest extent of the law.
Until accountability is enforced with zero tolerance, commercial greed and administrative apathy will continue at the expense of innocent lives that will continue to burn.

JCI Bangladesh honours 10 young achievers at TOYP 2026 gala
item.description:
JCI Bangladesh hosted the Ten Outstanding Young Persons (TOYP) of Bangladesh 2026 gala ceremony at the Grand Ballroom of Radisson Blu Dhaka on Saturday.
Presented by BioBuild Development Ltd and powered by Rhythm, the event celebrated young individuals recognised for their achievements, leadership and contributions to society.
Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee, MP, water resources minister, attended the ceremony as chief guest, while Swiss Ambassador to Bangladesh Reto Renggli was the special guest.
The event brought together distinguished guests and members of the JCI Bangladesh community to recognise young talent and celebrate leadership, achievement and social impact.
Arefeen Raafi Ahmed, national president of JCI Bangladesh for 2026, welcomed the guests and award recipients. Event adviser Erfan Haque and event directors Sk Motiur Rahman and Zafir Shafie expressed their gratitude to those involved.
The 10 TOYP award recipients this year were Dr Sunsila Jabrin Priyanka, MP, for Humanitarian Leadership; Mohammad Mohasin for Moral Leadership; Samanzar Sayeed for Culture; Amid Sakif Khan for Business Accomplishment; Lisa Saha for Academic Leadership; Kazi Ashikur Rasul for Entrepreneurial Accomplishment; Mohammad Jahirul Islam for Voluntary Leadership; Afeida Khandaker for Sports; Md Rasel Bin Ahad for Economic Development; and Afsan Ara Bindu for Personal Accomplishment.
The silver sponsors were Stamford University Bangladesh, Curtivelle, Mutual Logistics Solution, English Therapy, Seven Seas Shipping Lines, Eastern Medical College and Hospital, and Red Carpet.
Singularity Ltd was the creative partner, Crimson Cup the coffee partner, and Craftiman the gift partner. Zephyr and Lambert were the refreshment partners, while Hermizon was the fashion partner.
JCI Bangladesh is part of Junior Chamber International, a global network that empowers young people to create positive change through leadership development, community engagement and active citizenship.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 8th globally with ‘unhealthy’ air quality
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 8th among the world's most polluted cities on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 177 at 8:50am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 239, while Delhi in India ranked second with a score of 207, followed by Singapore in Singapore third place with an AQI score of 204.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: PSG fight back to beat Strasbourg after Dembele penalty miss
item.description:
Ousmane Dembele missed a penalty but later scored as Paris Saint-Germain produced a fightback to win 3-1 away at Strasbourg on Saturday and go to the top of the French Ligue 1 table.
PSG were trailing to an early goal by United States star Giovanni Reyna for Strasbourg at the Stade de la Meinau, and last year's Ballon d'Or winner Dembele came off the bench before he put a penalty wide in the 72nd minute.
But Dembele made amends in style, first by setting up Illia Zabarnyi to equalise in the 78th minute and then by putting the reigning French and European champions ahead with five minutes to go.
He then played a part in setting up Desire Doue for PSG's third in stoppage time, as Luis Enrique's men made it four straight Ligue 1 wins, and six on the bounce including the Champions League.
"I told him: 'If you play for 25 minutes and you give an assist and score a goal, you don't need to play any longer. That is enough'," Luis Enrique said of Dembele, one of a host of PSG players rested from the starting line-up in between key European games against Manchester City and Barcelona.
"Ousmane and the other players are not machines and they will not always be at their best. There are games over the course of a season where you are not at your best level because that is normal," added Luis Enrique.
After failing to win any of their first three domestic league matches this season, PSG are up to 14 points from seven games and are therefore top of the standings on goals scored from Lille as well as Monaco, before the principality club visit Lorient on Sunday.
Lille drew 1-1 with Brest, while Rennes, Paris FC and Lyon all have the opportunity to go back above PSG when they play on Sunday.
This game, one of PSG's toughest domestic tests of the season, fell awkwardly just three days after their 4-2 Champions League victory at City and three days before they host Barcelona.
True to form, Luis Enrique therefore made sweeping changes with eight in total from the City game. Dembele was one of those relegated to the bench here with an eye on the meeting with Barcelona, his former side.
Strasbourg sought to take advantage and went in front on 17 minutes when Reyna received a Gessime Yassine pass just inside the area, turned and beat Matvey Safonov low at the goalkeeper's near post.
The visitors were grateful to Safonov for a superb save to deny Conrad Harder just after half-time, before Luis Enrique sent on some of the cavalry, including Dembele and Doue.
They won a penalty after a VAR check confirmed that a Doue shot had hit the arm of Pape Demba Diop, but Dembele -- who scored a penalty in May's Champions League final win over Arsenal -- put his spot-kick wide. Three different PSG players have now missed penalties in their last three games.
"We have lots of players who can take them but it is true that we don't have one specialist," said Luis Enrique.
However, Dembele crossed from the right for Ukraine defender Zabarnyi to equalise with a cushioned close-range finish, and then controlled on the edge of the box before firing in to make it 2-1.
That was his first Ligue 1 goal this season to go with three in the Champions League, and Dembele -- who is nominated again for this year's Ballon d'Or -- then brought down a long Safonov kick before finding Ferran Torres who set up Doue to seal the win.
Lille were looking to bounce back from a 3-0 Champions League loss at Arsenal when they entertained Brest, but they needed a penalty from 40-year-old Olivier Giroud to get a 1-1 draw.
Lens, France's other Champions League representative, won 3-1 away at Troyes.

item.title: 'Best in world' Yamal powers Barca to Betis rout, Atletico strike late
item.description:
Barcelona coach Hansi Flick hailed Lamine Yamal as the best player in the world as his dominant side routed 10-man Real Betis 5-2 on Saturday to return five points clear at the top of La Liga.
Atletico, second, snatched a late 1-0 win at Espanyol, while third-placed Betis are eight points adrift of the leaders and Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla on Sunday.
Teenage winger Yamal scored a brilliant goal for Spanish champions Barca, with Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo also finding the net at La Cartuja stadium in Seville.
Betis had Facundo Bernal sent off for a headbutt on Yamal early in the second half of a pulsating clash.
Barca set a new club record for victories at the start of a league campaign and equalled the all-time record of nine, set by Real Madrid in the 1968/69 season. Flick's side boast 11 wins from 11 games across all competitions.
Yamal, who is hoping to be crowned the world's best player at the Ballon d'Or ceremony later in October, got the ball rolling with a spectacular opener.
"I think it was an amazing match for the fans, and all the people who love football, it was amazing," Flick told reporters.
"Lamine today, when you see the first goal he scored, unbelievable, this is for me, at the moment the best player in the world."
Yamal, 19, turned sharply on the edge of the box to escape Bernal and then exquisitely curled into the top corner in the 10th minute.
"(It was) an incredible goal, we've got used to him doing this lately, I have to say," Rodri told DAZN.
"In the end, players like that make the difference. But I try to focus on the other things he brings... (like) hard work, a lot of solidarity with the team, understanding the game and where he could find space."
Despite their irresistible attacking play, Barca's clear weakness under Flick has been their defence and Betis were level before the half-hour mark through a Valentin Gomez header.
Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri put Barca back in front with a header from a corner, before Giovani Lo Celso thought he had equalised in spectacular fashion for the hosts.
However, the Argentine midfielder's long-range goal was ruled out for a handball by Cucho Hernandez earlier in the move, much to Betis' chagrin.
Jesus extended Barca's lead six minutes into the second half from Yamal's cut-back, moments after having another goal ruled out for offside.
Ez Abde immediately pulled one back for Betis during a wild spell, and in the aftermath they were reduced to 10 men when Bernal was sent off for a headbutt on Yamal, who was booked for his part in a confrontation between several players from both sides.
Garcia finished from close range for Barca's fourth and Raphinha came off the bench after missing the previous two matches injured, with Flick taking off Yamal to prevent a potential suspension for the Clasico next weekend.
"With this result, we have to change him," said Flick. "I (told him) I'm very proud of him because he played a fantastic game."
Substitute Olmo finished the match off with a neat finish from the edge of the box as Betis backed off to allow Barca's attention to turn to Europe, where they face Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.
Earlier, Alex Baena struck in the 89th minute to snatch Atletico Madrid their narrow win at Espanyol.
Spain international Baena smashed home from the edge of the box to claim the Rojiblancos an important late victory from a tight game in Cornella.
Atletico have won six consecutive games across all competitions.
Baena, who struggled last season but has been in fine fettle since winning the World Cup with Spain this summer, hugged coach Diego Simeone after finding the net.
"The World Cup took him to a different place, he sees football differently than others and (now) he's more confident and stronger, he's the player we went looking for," Simeone told reporters after Baena's fifth league goal of the campaign.

item.title: Haaland stars in Man City win, Liverpool beat Brentford
item.description:
Erling Haaland starred with a double as Premier League leaders Manchester City beat Ipswich 3-2, while Liverpool came from behind to seal a 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday.
City are in turmoil off the pitch after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
On the grass they have made a perfect start, with seven successive league victories marking their best opening to a Premier League season.
City, who are appealing against the guilty verdict after branding it a "Premier League conspiracy", sit six points clear of champions Arsenal.
Second-placed Arsenal can close the gap with a win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.
With City potentially facing a massive points deduction or even expulsion from the top flight if their appeal fails, it remains to be seen whether their results will even matter by the end of the season.
For now, Enzo Maresca's side are in fine form after bouncing back from their midweek loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.
There was a defiant mood at the Etihad Stadium, where City fans booed the Premier League anthem before kick-off, while thousands waved inflatable bananas to underline their commitment to the club regardless of its plight.
City supporters took toy bananas to matches to lighten the mood when the team was struggling in the late 1980s.
Phil Foden put Maresca's men ahead in the 19th minute with a sharp turn and finish after Jeremy Doku's incisive run prised open the Ipswich defence.
Foden's first goal this season was followed by an Ipswich equaliser in the 21st minute when Daizen Maeda evaded Marc Guehi to fire home.
Haaland restored City's lead in the 34th minute with a pin-point header from Mateo Kovacic's cross.
Haaland killed off Ipswich in the 69th minute, sprinting onto Iliman Ndiaye's pass and steering his shot past Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton.
Zian Flemming's 90th-minute penalty, awarded for a foul by Guehi, set up a tense finale but City held on.
"Very happy with today's game, we controlled it for 95 minutes. We create chances, we score. We finish a little bit suffering together but overall, it is good," Maresca said.
In west London, Liverpool were stunned when Brentford defender Keane Lewis-Potter looped a header past Alisson Becker from Igor Thiago's cross in the 44th minute.
But the Bees were reduced to 10 men in first half stoppage-time after Yehor Yarmolyuk's head made contact with Jeremy Jacquet's face while they waited for a corner.
Liverpool lost Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong to injuries, but still made their numerical advantage count in the 62nd minute.
Victor Munoz cut inside and slotted a composed equaliser past Brentford's former Liverpool keeper Caoimhin Kelleher.
Alexander Isak blasted Liverpool's winner in the 70th minute after Barcola teed up the Sweden striker for his fifth goal this term.
Brentford finished with nine men following Vitaly Janelt's second booking in stoppage-time.
Beaten by City in their previous league game, Liverpool are up to fifth place after inflicting Brentford's first league defeat of the season.
"You see the results of Brentford at home and you have to be ready for these kinds of battles. We had 45 minutes to do the comeback and I think we played really well," Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said.
Pedro Neto's double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as fourth-placed Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez to a head injury.
Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half and secured the points during stoppage-time.
The Argentine international was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital.
Fulham won for the first time in the league this season as Alex Iwobi's 33rd-minute goal clinched a 1-0 victory against Hull at Craven Cottage.
Alvaro Arbeloa's side moved out of the relegation zone despite having Ryan Sessegnon sent off for a crude lunge on Robinio Vaz in the final minutes.
Newcastle host Aston Villa in Saturday's late game.

item.title: Messi scores twice, provides assist as Inter Miami beat Atlanta United 3-1
item.description:
Lionel Messi scored twice and provided an assist as Inter Miami cruised to a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United in Major League Soccer (MLS) on Saturday.
Germán Berterame opened the scoring in the final minute of the first half, converting a move set up by Messi and Luis Suárez to put Miami ahead.
Messi then scored twice in four minutes, finding the net in the 56th and 60th minutes to extend Miami’s lead to 3-0. Berterame assisted on both goals, while Suárez provided an assist on Messi’s second strike.
With his 15th assist of the season, Messi drew level with Los Angeles FC’s Son Heung-min at the top of the league’s assist standings. He also became the first player in MLS history to record at least 15 assists in three consecutive seasons.
The Argentine star’s goals took his league-leading tally to 25. He won the Golden Boot last season with 29 goals and, alongside Josef Martínez, is one of only two players in MLS history to score at least 25 goals in two regular seasons.
Messi now has 40 goal contributions this season, nine short of Carlos Vela’s MLS record of 49, set with Los Angeles FC in 2019. Miami have four matches remaining.
Berterame has recorded eight assists, while Suárez registered a career-high 11th assist.
Atlanta pulled one back in the 89th minute when Fafà Picault converted a penalty. Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair made two saves, while Atlanta’s Lucas Hoyos also stopped two shots.
Atlanta had played out a 2-2 draw with Miami at home earlier in September.
Inter Miami will visit the New York Red Bulls next Saturday, while Atlanta United will host Chicago Fire.

item.title: Zimbabwe beat Bangladesh in tri-series opener
item.description:
Bangladesh were bowled out for 172 in 33.4 overs while chasing 272, losing to Zimbabwe by 99 runs in the opening match of the tri-series in Abu Dhabi on Saturday.
The defeat exposed Bangladesh’s batting frailties once again.
After reaching 42 without loss in the first six overs, they lost wickets in clusters and never recovered, with Tanzid Hasan Tamim’s 46 and Saif Hassan’s 26 among the few notable contributions.
Soumya Sarkar was the first to go, caught off Blessing Muzarabani for nine off 17 balls.
Tanzid kept the scoring moving but fell for 46 after surviving a dropped catch the previous delivery. Ryan Burl took the catch at point.
Najmul Hossain Shanto followed, trapped lbw by Brad Evans, before captain Towhid Hridoy fell for 13 off 21 balls to Sikandar Raza.
Raza had to review the decision after the on-field umpire turned down his appeal.
Mosaddek Hossain was also dismissed lbw, this time by Wellington Masakadza, leaving Bangladesh five wickets down and still needing 160 runs.
Saif offered some resistance before falling for 26. Rishad Hossain made 23, but Zimbabwe wrapped up the innings in 33.4 overs.
Earlier, Zimbabwe recovered from a poor start to post 271 for eight in their 50 overs after winning the toss and batting first.
Taskin Ahmed tore through the top order, taking three wickets in the opening seven overs as Zimbabwe slipped to 24 for three.
But Craig Ervine and Brendan Taylor turned the innings around with a 150-run partnership for the fourth wicket.
Taylor scored 81 off 101 balls, while Ervine made 93 off 106, hitting nine fours. Their partnership took Zimbabwe past 150 and put them in a position to set Bangladesh a challenging target.
Saif broke the stand by dismissing Taylor with a catch off a reverse sweep, then removed Sikandar Raza in his next over. Ervine continued until Shoriful Islam had him caught behind, nine runs short of a century. Shoriful later dismissed Brad Evans to finish with two wickets for 47 runs.
Taskin took three for 44, while Saif claimed two for 17. Zimbabwe’s lower order added valuable runs at the end, with Wellington Masakadza and Newman Nyamhuri putting on an unbeaten 37 for the ninth wicket. Nyamhuri finished on 21 not out.

item.description:
There is a distinct atmosphere in Dhaka’s commercial hubs these days—a quiet, watchful patience mixed with systemic exhaustion.
Walking through the financial corridors, the bustling trade depots of Chittagong, or the readymade garment (RMG) belts of Gazipur, one senses an economy caught in an uncomfortable posture: suspended between necessary, painful reform and a stubborn, lingering stagnation.
The recent economic indicators underline this caution.
While consumer price pressures saw a slight moderation, the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation remained uncomfortably elevated at 9.92%—with food inflation staying above 10%.
On the trade front, monthly export inflows dropped by approximately 4.5% year-on-year to $3.63 billion, reflecting supply-chain disruptions and temporary labor unrest across major manufacturing hubs.
Coupled with subdued industrial output, constrained private sector credit growth, and depressed Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) readings, these figures illustrate how high interest rates—maintained via a tight monetary stance—continue to weigh on near-term domestic expansion.
Underpinning these macroeconomic headwinds is a long-standing balance sheet crisis: the sheer weight of distressed assets suffocating the banking sector.
Following rigorous post-transition audits and the unwinding of regulatory forbearance, official central bank figures revealed that non-performing loans (NPLs) soared to unprecedented heights—surpassing 30% of total loan disbursements.
This sharp surge does not represent sudden structural collapse, but rather a overdue accounting of reality.
For years, loose re-scheduling policies, hidden related-party lending, and artificial classification concessions masked the true scale of bad debts.
Unveiling these stressed assets has constrained commercial bank liquidity, tied up vital capital reserves, and sharply restricted fresh lending to productive private enterprises.
Yet, reading these figures purely as signs of distress misses the broader context.
What Bangladesh is experiencing is not a sudden downward spiral, but rather the structural friction of an economy undergoing essential stabilization.
For decades, macro-level stability in Bangladesh rested on a delicate equilibrium: steady export growth, resilient remittance inflows, and tight management of the local currency.
However, global inflationary shocks, coupled with legacy financial sector stress, brought significant external account pressure and depleted foreign exchange reserves.
To stem these imbalances, monetary policy was shifted toward discipline, keeping policy rates elevated and moving toward greater exchange rate flexibility to protect external liquidity.
The first critical stage of recovery requires prioritizing macroeconomic defense over rapid growth.
During this phase, monetary authorities hold benchmark interest rates high to rein in excess liquidity, curb import demand, and build up foreign exchange buffers.
While this policy holding pattern creates short-term pressure on business expansion and consumer demand, it is essential for stopping the depletion of reserves and anchoring broader economic expectations.
As external accounts stabilize, the economy transitions into a second phase of structural repair and balance sheet cleanup.
Here, the focus shifts toward taming persistent food and core inflation while carrying out deeply needed banking sector reforms.
By addressing non-performing loans, restoring fiscal discipline, and reforming tax administration, this intermediate stage clears out institutional bottlenecks and sets a clean regulatory baseline for local and foreign investors alike.
Only after inflation cools and financial sector stability is restored can the economy return to a sustainable, high-growth trajectory.
In this final phase, lower borrowing costs allow private sector credit growth to accelerate safely.
Supported by export diversification, green manufacturing practices, and structural infrastructure investments, the economy reclaims its momentum on far healthier, non-inflationary fundamentals.

As highlighted in the table, foreign exchange buffers have stabilized into a firmer position, supported by steady remittance streams and calibrated import management.
Rather than rapid drainage, reserves now present a defensible moat against external trade shocks.
The current slowdown is not a policy failure; it is the natural, calculated price of restoring macro-financial stability after prolonged distortions.
The logic of interim stewardship
To understand where Bangladesh stands today, it is instructive to look back at previous transitional periods in the nation’s economic history.
During prior non-partisan interim regimes—most notably the 2007–2008 administration—the primary institutional objective was rarely rapid, unsustainable GDP expansion.
Instead, those periods focused on system cleanup, administrative rationalization, and structural repair.
Interim tenures operate under a fundamentally different mandate than elected political governments:
The friction seen today echoes those historic stabilization phases.
Restructuring financial institutions, enforcing tighter capital adequacy ratios, and curtailing informal capital flight feel restrictive while underway.
However, history demonstrates that these periods of policy tightening serve as necessary resets. They clear accumulated balance sheet distress, establishing a far sounder foundation for subsequent expansion.
Foundation for resilience
An economy is a complex, adaptive machine. Short-term data points often reflect past imbalances rather than future potential.
While headline metrics remain challenging, several structural pillars underscore Bangladesh’s underlying strength:
Transitioning from stabilization to renewed growth will not happen overnight. It requires patience as monetary tightening gradually brings inflation under control and banking reforms clear out bad assets.
But as historical precedent shows, economies built on sound fundamentals do not remain stagnant forever.

Bangladesh's current adjustment phase is laying the groundwork for a more resilient, sustainable recovery over the long horizon.

item.title: Navigating the NEIR dilemma
item.description:
The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) is preparing for its most consequential attempt yet to implement the National Equipment Identity Register (NEIR).
Slated for January 1, 2027, this centralized database tracks International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers across all mobile networks to neutralize illicit handsets, curtail smuggling, and plug massive revenue leaks.
However, the path to enforcement is fraught with history. Past rollouts have triggered intense resistance, protests, and even violent clashes at the BTRC headquarters.
As authorities gear up for a phased implementation, the fundamental question remains: Can regulators balance national security and state revenue with consumer affordability and industry survival, or will history repeat itself?
The BTRC said around 770.6 million IMEI numbers were stored in the NEIR system as of June 2026, including about 411.8 million on the grey list, meaning unauthorized devices.
It cautioned that IMEI numbers cannot be treated as the number of handsets because a single phone may have multiple IMEIs, while cloned IMEIs can be used in several devices.
Backed by recommendations from the National Security Intelligence (NSI), the Ministry of Home Affairs, and the National Board of Revenue (NBR)—which estimates a staggering Tk2,000 crore annual loss from tax evasion on unauthorized handsets—the BTRC has structured a two-phase rollout:
The protests and the controversy
The road to NEIR has been defined by policy whiplash and public friction. Initially conceptualized in 2021, subsequent target dates—including announcements for late 2025 and early 2026—were repeatedly delayed or walked back following severe pushback.
When implementation was previously pushed forward, it unleashed fierce opposition from the Mobile Business Community Bangladesh (MBCB) and independent retailers.
Traders staged demonstrations, blocked roads in Agargaon and across Dhaka, and rallied against policies they argued would devastate small businesses.
The tension boiled over when frustrated retailers and stakeholders marched on the BTRC building, resulting in localized vandalism and property damage.
Retail users have echoed these concerns from a consumer standpoint.
Critics argue that forcing consumers away from affordable, high-spec grey-market devices—while official channels heavily promote expensive or lower-spec alternatives—disproportionately penalizes budget-restricted buyers.
As consumer sentiment often frames it, restrictive policies risk creating a captive market that leaves everyday citizens paying more for less.
Faiz Ahmed Taiyeb, for special assistant for the ministry of posts, telecommunications, and IT to the interim government’s chief adviser, told the media earlier this year: “We are implementing NEIR purely in the interest of maintaining state discipline and security."
"When a regulatory tool comes, various problems arise. We have resolved these problems very quickly... A team has worked 24/7 (every day of the week). They have worked through the night and resolved the problems."
Major official manufacturers have taken a more calculated stance.
Ziauddin Chowdhury, country general manager of Xiaomi Technologies Bangladesh Private Limited, welcomed the decision, emphasizing that a sustainable NEIR policy is vital for a structured market.
Smartphone prices are rising globally. In this context, implementing NEIR while maintaining a high import duty of around 61.80% risks pushing smartphones beyond the reach of ordinary consumers. If the government is later compelled to suspend or roll back NEIR under public pressure, it would undermine the credibility of the policy itself. A balanced duty structure must therefore be established from the outset, he also said.
“Frequent policy changes also discourage foreign investors. It is essential that this initiative be consumer-friendly and business-friendly. We envision a smartphone market where consumers can access products at fair prices, the government collects its due revenue, and all businesses have the opportunity to operate through legitimate channels,” Chowdhury added.
MBCB vice-president Shamim Mollah said traders wanted an opportunity to import handsets under a regulatory framework and called for lower taxes.
‘Give us a chance to provide input as well. Reduce the tax, give us the opportunity to import,’ he said.
Mollah also demanded provisions allowing traders to import used phones after paying taxes.

item.title: DSCC launches New Market drive to curb dengue, clear footpaths
item.description:
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has launched a special drive in the New Market area to intensify cleaning activities and clear footpaths as part of efforts to prevent dengue.
DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam led the drive after inaugurating the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme on Saturday. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inspected cleaning and mosquito-control activities in DSCC areas as part of the government’s weekly “Cleaning Day” programme aimed at preventing dengue.
During a surprise inspection on Saturday morning, the prime minister visited Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, the Green Road Government Staff Quarters and the government residential area in Azimpur.
Speaking to students at Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, Tarique Rahman stressed the importance of environmental protection, dengue prevention and maintaining cleanliness. He also encouraged students to plant trees to help reduce environmental pollution.
At the Green Road and Azimpur residential areas, he spoke with residents and urged them to keep their surroundings clean and remove stagnant water to prevent dengue.
He also inspected cleanliness activities along the main roads and surrounding areas and instructed officials to take necessary measures.
Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives State Minister Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Abu Abdullah Md Saleh, DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam and senior government officials accompanied the prime minister during the inspections.
The DSCC said special cleaning drives were conducted simultaneously in all 75 wards as part of the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme. City corporation cleaners and mosquito-control workers, along with local residents, took part in the campaign. Awareness rallies and microphone announcements were also organised throughout the day in different wards to encourage public participation.

item.title: Metro rail's Motijheel to Kamalapur expected to open in July next year
item.description:
The much-anticipated extension of Metro Rail's MRT Line-6 from Motijheel to Kamalapur is expected to open for commercial operations in July next year.
“The overall physical progress of the civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension of MRT Line-6 has reached 84.85%,” Project Director of the Dhaka Mass Transit Development Project (MRT Line-6), Brigadier General (Retd) Md Abdul Wohab, told BSS here on Saturday.
He said mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) works at Kamalapur station are underway, while equipment manufactured abroad will be installed soon after being brought into the country.
According to project details, electro-mechanical works on the extension have progressed by 58%, while construction of the 1.16-kilometre viaduct on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension has been completed, and it has been handed over to Contract Package-7 (CP-07) for rail track installation.
The structural work on Kamalapur MRT Station has also been completed, while MEP and architectural works are underway and are expected to be finished by December 31, 2026.
Meanwhile, work on seven integrated electro-mechanical subsystems under CP-07 is progressing. These include electrical and track systems, signaling, automatic fare collection (AFC), platform screen doors (PSD), telecommunications, lifts and escalators.
The 21.26-kilometre MRT Line-6, extending from Uttara North to Kamalapur, is progressing towards completion. As of September 30, 2026, the physical progress of the Uttara North-Motijheel section stood at 99.67%, while civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension had reached 84.85%.
Once the final section becomes operational, MRT Line-6 will connect Uttara North (Diabari) directly to Kamalapur Railway Station, completing the full 21.26-kilometre route.
The line will have 17 stations, including major stops at Mirpur-10, Agargaon, Farmgate and Dhaka University.
The metro rail began operating on the Uttara–Agargaon section on December 28, 2022. The Agargaon–Motijheel section opened on November 4, 2023. Since the Motijheel section opened, the metro rail has become a vital transport link for Dhaka residents, serving thousands of commuters daily.
Under the current schedule, the first trains depart from Motijheel at 7am and Uttara North at 6:40am.
On average, more than 0.4 million passengers have travelled on the metro rail since its launch, while on September 10, over 0.5 million passengers travelled on the metro, according to project information.
Revenue from ticket sales is also increasing as passenger numbers grow.

item.description:
A parliamentary standing committee on the Planning Ministry has decided to investigate the implementation of the Karnaphuli Tunnel project and the reasons behind its current financial losses.
The committee took the decision at its second meeting at the National Parliament on Saturday.
The committee discussed the tunnel’s feasibility study, implementation process and financial losses, and decided to hold a detailed discussion on the matter at its next meeting.
It also unanimously agreed to examine the project’s implementation and financial losses through a proper investigation, with the relevant authorities expected to provide the committee with necessary assistance.
The meeting also reviewed delays in development projects under the Planning Ministry and the reasons for extending their implementation periods.
According to the ministry, the implementation periods of 256 projects were extended in the 2025-26 fiscal year.
The ministry attributed the extensions to complications in land acquisition, dependence on imports, difficulties in appointing project directors, inadequate feasibility studies, delays in releasing funds and conflicts between ministries, among other factors.
The committee recommended effective measures by the relevant authorities to address these problems and reduce delays in project implementation.
In line with an earlier decision, the ministry also provided members with a list of 1,153 ongoing projects under its jurisdiction and presented their five-year strategic plans, explaining how the projects are being implemented.
The ministry informed the committee that work was under way to formulate a new policy for appointing project directors.
It expressed hope that the policy, once finalized, would help resolve persistent problems in the appointment process.
The meeting was also informed that efforts are being made to address regional disparities in project implementation and ensure equitable development of rural infrastructure.
Regarding staffing, the ministry said recruitment of 65 officers and employees across different grades is at the final stage against 221 vacant posts.

item.title: FSCD DG: All 538 fire stations prepared for emergencies during Durga Puja
item.description:
Fire Service and Civil Defense (FSCD) has taken comprehensive measures to ensure fire safety at Durga Puja venues across the country, with all 538 fire stations ready to respond to emergencies during the festival.
Director General of Fire Service and Civil Defense Brigadier General Sultanul Afreen Junaid disclosed the preparations at a press conference held at the department’s headquarters in Dhaka on Saturday.
He said fire stations would remain on standby throughout the festival, monitoring fire safety at puja mandaps in their respective areas and maintaining round-the-clock communication with local administrations and puja committees.
During inspections, fire service personnel will assess fire risks and advise organizers on measures to address them.
They will also publicize the telephone numbers of nearby fire stations and the 102 hotlines for emergency assistance, he added.
Temporary fire stations operating in different locations will remain on high alert, while officials at divisional, district and zonal levels will stay on standby to inspect puja venues and respond to emergencies.
The director general also said the central control room and all divisional control rooms would operate round the clock. Upon receiving an emergency call, they would direct one or more nearby fire stations to respond immediately.
All divisional and district offices, along with fire stations, will coordinate continuously with local administrations and take necessary decisions and implement measures in line with their directions, he said.
At immersion sites, the department will deploy personnel and volunteers, road rescue equipment and ambulances. Lighting units will also be deployed at night where necessary.
Control rooms will be maintained at the department’s headquarters and divisional and district headquarters to ensure continuous communication with fire stations under their respective jurisdictions.
Calling for greater public awareness, Sultanul Afreen said, “Awareness is protection,” and sought the media’s cooperation in raising awareness about fire safety alongside the department’s own efforts.

item.title: Legal notice seeks probe into possible use of dengue as biological weapon
item.description:
A legal notice has been served on the government seeking a high-level scientific investigation into the unusually high dengue mortality in Bangladesh and possible genetic mutations of the virus, including an inquiry into allegations that it could be linked to a covert biological attack.
The notice also demands the establishment of an internationally accredited research laboratory to prevent and investigate biological weapons threats.
Supreme Court lawyer Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun served the notice on Saturday in the public interest.
It was addressed to the secretaries of the ministries of defence, home affairs, health and family welfare, and foreign affairs, as well as the administrators of Dhaka North and South city corporations. A copy was also sent to the United Nations resident coordinator in Bangladesh.
The notice describes dengue as a severe public health crisis rather than a routine illness, arguing that the recurring deaths and growing number of cases warrant investigation beyond conventional mosquito-control measures.
Citing books on biological warfare and medical research, Mamun, who is also studying for a Master of Public Health degree, refers to historical accounts of plans to use disease-carrying insects in biological attacks.
The notice cites The A to Z of Nuclear, Biological, and Chemical Warfare (2019), by Benjamin C Garrett and John Hart, which discusses a Japanese military plan during World War II, codenamed “Operation PX”. According to the notice, the plan involved releasing insects carrying pathogens linked to dengue, plague, cholera and typhus along the US coast.
It also refers to Anthony Tu’s book Chemical and Biological Weapons and Terrorism (2018), which the notice says discusses the classification of dengue virus among biological agents considered for weaponisation by the US military.
Another reference is Advances in Biological and Chemical Terrorism Countermeasures (2008), edited by Ronald J Kendall and other experts. The notice cites the publication in support of its concerns about the potential misuse of disease-causing agents.
The notice argues that Bangladesh’s high population density and mosquito prevalence, alongside the reported severity of recent dengue outbreaks, warrant an urgent scientific and forensic investigation. It calls for epidemiologists, virologists and public health specialists to examine the virus’s genetic characteristics, origin and transmission mechanisms to determine whether there is evidence of deliberate or artificial modification.
However, the notice does not present evidence establishing that the dengue outbreak in Bangladesh resulted from a biological attack.
Mamun also cites Bangladesh’s obligations under international law, noting that the country is a signatory to the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC). He refers to Articles I and X of the convention, which prohibit biological weapons and address the peaceful use of biological science, as well as United Nations Security Council Resolution 1540 of 2004, which requires states to take measures against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.
The notice further invokes Articles 18(1) and 32 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, concerning the state’s responsibility to improve public health and the right to life.
It asks the authorities to arrange an expert-led genetic and forensic investigation into the dengue virus within 10 days to assess whether there is any evidence of an artificial biological attack. It also calls for the immediate establishment of a high-security laboratory for research into biological weapons prevention and comprehensive, science-based measures to control Aedes mosquitoes.
The notice warns that failure to meet the demands could lead to a public interest litigation petition before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court under Article 102 of the Constitution, seeking measures to protect public health, national security and citizens’ lives.

item.title: Russia hails Trump waiving sanctions as ‘historic’
item.description:
Russia on Saturday hailed US President Donald Trump’s move to waive new sanctions on it as “historic,” as Ukraine worries he is taking Moscow’s side in Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.
Trump signed an executive order Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia’s energy revenues amid a clash with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The decision came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine -- especially its capital, Kyiv -- in the fifth year of its offensive, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
“The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment,” Kirill Dmitriev, envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, said on social media.
The Lindsey Graham Act -- named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill -- targeted Russia’s energy and defense sectors, as well as Putin and the so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers used by Moscow to circumvent Western sanctions.
The Kremlin and Putin have not yet reacted to the move, which is a major diplomatic win for Moscow.
Dmitriev said the act would have caused “serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets.”
Trump’s waiver comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease existing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.
He announced the executive order Friday, shortly after Putin appeared in military uniform and said Moscow aims to capture the rest of east Ukraine.
US-led talks to end the war in Ukraine have not led to a breakthrough. Both Putin and Zelensky have frustrated Trump in the past with a lack of progress in halting the grinding war.
The move is bound to spook Ukraine’s European allies, who worry the White House is taking the Kremlin’s side.
Zelensky rallied his allies Friday on a visit to Brussels for a European Union summit, urging them to keep financing Ukraine’s fight and insisting he was standing up for his country amid the row with Trump.
Russian forces struck Ukraine’s southern city of Kherson Saturday after Trump’s announcement, killing one person and wounding 22, local officials said.
Russia has increased strikes on Kyiv in recent weeks, squeezing the city as Ukrainians brace for another winter of war.
Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defenses ahead of winter.
Russia controls large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine and Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine by force.
“On the whole I see a positive trend in the operations of the troop groupings,” Putin told army leaders Friday, dressed in military attire.
“Undoubtedly, one of the main objectives remains the liberation of the Donetsk People’s Republic,” he added, using the Kremlin’s name for the eastern Donetsk region.
European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky Friday as he grappled with Trump.
“This is no time to withdraw support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions,” said European Council chief Antonio Costa.
“Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure.”
European concerns have been heightened by disruptions to a critical US-provided satellite system that has hampered Ukraine’s ability to counter Russia’s intense bombardments.

Dhaka's air quality remains 'unhealthy'
item.description:
The air quality in Dhaka remained unhealthy on Saturday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 166 at 9:14am.
With this score, the capital ranked ninth among the world's most polluted cities.
Iraq’s Baghdad, Singapore’s Singapore, Pakistan’s Lahore and India’s Mumbai occupied the top four spots on the list, with AQI scores of 378, 206, 201 and 192, respectively.
An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with an acceptable air quality, while one between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy."
AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Former additional secretary found dead at Officers Club
item.description:
The body of former additional secretary Md Mosharraf Hossain was recovered from a building under construction at the Officers Club in Dhaka’s Ramna area on Friday morning.
Police recovered the body around 11:45am.
Mosharraf Hossain, a member of the Officers Club, lived with his family in Banani.
According to reports, he arrived at the club around 10am with his youngest daughter. He left her near the swimming pool, beside the building under construction, and entered the structure.
About an hour later, his body was found in a bloodied condition on the ground floor near a staircase.
Sheikh Zahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Ramna division, said Mosharraf had poor eyesight and apparently fell from the third floor into an open space on the ground floor.
“We have completed the preliminary examination of the body,” he said.
The deputy commissioner said the family had requested that no post-mortem examination be conducted and that the body would be handed over to them.
Mosharraf’s eldest daughter lives in the United States. According to the family, his burial will take place after she arrives in Bangladesh.

item.title: Dengue: Four more die, 1,181 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Four people died of dengue, and 1,181 were hospitalized after being infected with dengue in the last 24 hours till 8am on Friday, according to a regular report of Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With four deaths in the past 24 hours, the death toll from the disease stood at 335 this year.
Of the newly hospitalized dengue patients, 410 were in Dhaka Division, 92 in Mymensingh Division, 242 in Chittagong Division, 140 in Khulna Division, 99 in Rajshahi, 71 in Rangpur Division and 127 in Barisal Division.
According to the report, a total of 108,440 dengue patients have so far been hospitalized across the country this year.
However, in the last 24 hours, 1,179 patients recovered and were discharged from hospitals.
So far, 102,210 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the disease last year.

Four die after gas cylinder blast in Narayanganj
item.description:
All four people who suffered burn injuries in a gas cylinder blast in Kachpur, Narayanganj, have died, including a husband and wife.
The latest victim, Rony, 19, died while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka on Friday morning.
Dr Sultan Mahmud Shikder of the institute confirmed his death.
Earlier, Rozina, 30, died on the afternoon of October 14. Her husband Sharif, 34, died early on October 15, while her brother Riaz, 22, died later that day.
Rozina suffered burns to 60% of her body, while Sharif and Riaz sustained burns to 40% each. Rony had burns covering 70% of his body.
The blast occurred around 1:30am on October 10 in a room on the second floor of a six-storey building in Sonapur, Kachpur.
Four people were severely burned in the explosion, which was reportedly caused by a gas cylinder leak.
The victims were identified as tenant Rozina, her husband Sharif, her brother Riaz and another tenant, Rony.
Hearing the blast, local residents rushed to the scene and rescued the victims before taking them to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka for treatment.

item.title: National Parliament committee proposes annual assessments to enhance education quality
item.description:
The Standing Committee on the Ministry of Education of the 13th National Parliament has recommended introducing an annual assessment system aligned with international standards to improve quality of education and move beyond artificial competition over pass rates.
At its first meeting held at the National Parliament Building on September 10, the committee proposed a series of measures to ensure transparency in education spending, tackle irregularities and corruption, investigate declining secondary-level enrolment, strengthen teacher training and expand technical education.
Chairman of the committee and Member of Parliament Md Salim Bhuiyan told Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS) at the Secretariat yesterday that the previous government had focused on numerical indicators and pass rates rather than genuine educational quality.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government does not believe in this artificial competition. We want to ensure genuine quality in education in the country,” he said.
He stressed the need for annual assessments, a modern curriculum and evaluations of learning outcomes at three- or six-month intervals to bring students in line with international standards.
Further recommendations and details of the government's education roadmap will be presented at a press conference, he added.
Committee member Reza Kibria also emphasized setting specific annual benchmarks to ensure Bangladeshi students perform competitively in international assessments, particularly in mathematics and science.
Members proposed a long-term national education vision, modelled on Malaysia, to prevent frequent changes to education policies, curricula and textbooks following changes in government.
According to the meeting minutes, the government has proposed a budget of Tk57,301.68 crore for the Secondary and Higher Education Division in the 2026-27 fiscal year, 42.7% higher than the previous revised budget.
The initiatives discussed included distributing laptops to approximately 40,000 students who achieved a Golden GPA in 2026 and bringing seven million female students under a Tk4,000 crore scholarship program to promote girls’ education and reduce dropout rates.
The committee also acknowledged the transfer of outstanding dues to the bank accounts of around 70,000 retired teachers and employees through the Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) and iBAS systems.
In the initial phase, each teacher is receiving an average of Tk5 lakh.
The committee thanked Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for providing Tk2,000 crore in special assistance to address the crisis involving teachers' welfare and retirement benefits.
It recommended expediting MPO enlistment for eligible non-MPO institutions and long-serving teachers, reducing bureaucratic delays and investigating the significant decline in secondary-level enrolment.
Technical and Madrasah Education Division Secretary (routine charge) Shamsur Rahman Khan informed the meeting that technical education enrolment reached 19.16% in 2025, with a target of 30% by 2030.
Other decisions included field visits by committee members to inspect educational institutions, mandatory attendance of education board heads and National University representatives at future meetings, and faster settlement of outstanding allowances, subject to budget availability.
Educationists have welcomed the proposals, particularly the shift towards measurable learning outcomes and international standards, as potentially significant steps towards improving education quality.

item.title: Speakers: Climate-vulnerable countries must not be pushed into debt trap
item.description:
Climate-vulnerable countries must not be pushed into a new debt trap in the name of climate adaptation, speakers said at a human chain program in Mongla on Friday.
They said developed countries and corporations continue to profit from fossil fuel-dependent economies, while farmers, workers and climate-vulnerable nations bear the brunt of cyclones, droughts, river erosion and crop losses.
The speakers called for a just transition to green energy, environmental protection, climate justice and public ownership of resources.
The human chain program was held at Mithekhali Bazar in Mongla, coinciding with the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, scheduled for October 12-18. The event focused on the question of whose interests the global economy serves.
Dharitri Rakkhay Amra, Pashur River Waterkeeper, Udayan Youth Sangha, and Waterkeepers Bangladesh jointly organised the program.
Nur Alam Sheikh, a central leader of DHORA and Pashur River Waterkeeper, presided over the event. Speakers included Prof Nazrul Islam, labour leader Nazmul Haque, DHORA leader Molla Al Mamun, farmer leader Asaduzzaman Tito, SM Jane Alam Babu of Udayan Youth Sangha, youth leaders Sheikh Sifatullah Shuvo and Arafat Durjoy, and Mehedi Hasan of Waterkeepers Bangladesh.
Nazmul Haque said developing countries were struggling to repay foreign loans and interest while meeting essential spending needs in education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection. High interest rates, rising energy prices and climate-related disasters were further aggravating the crisis, he said.
“If people’s fundamental rights are curtailed to repay loans, who is development for?” he asked, stressing that public needs must take precedence over lenders’ conditions.
In his address, Nur Alam Sheikh said communities affected by climate change should receive fair compensation, not loans, for the losses and damage they suffer. “We must build a world for people, not for profit,” he said, calling for adequate climate financing and investment in renewable energy.
He also urged the government to ensure that food was treated as a fundamental human right rather than a source of corporate profit, promote environmentally friendly agriculture and ensure a just transition to green energy.
“Financing renewable energy is financing climate action,” he said, calling for an immediate shift to renewable energy.

item.title: Durga Puja begins in Gopalganj, Sunamganj with festive fervour
item.description:
The five-day Sharadiya Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community, began in Gopalganj on Friday with Maha Shashthi rituals, including the invocation and ceremonial welcome of the goddess.
According to the traditional calendar, this year's celebrations will continue for six days, ending on Wednesday, with Bijoya Dashami and the immersion of idols.
The festivities began gathering momentum on Thursday evening, when temples and puja mandaps across the district were illuminated with colourful lights and decorated with elaborate pandals, ornate gates and eye-catching designs. The sound of drums and conch shells added to the festive atmosphere as devotees visited the mandaps to offer prayers, take photographs and celebrate.
Priests performed Shashthi rituals on Friday morning, formally welcoming Goddess Durga to the mortal world from her heavenly abode on Mount Kailash, accompanied by her four children — Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik and Ganesha.
The goddess's face will be unveiled at the mandaps on Saturday, marking Maha Saptami. Saptami rituals will continue tomorrow, followed by Ashtami on Monday, Navami on Tuesday and Dashami on Wednesday.
This year, Durga Puja is being celebrated at 1,288 mandaps across Gopalganj's five upazilas and four municipalities. Security has been strengthened at the venues to ensure peaceful celebrations.
Sanjay Sikdar, general secretary of the Gopalganj district unit of the Puja Udjapan Parishad, said devotees would bid farewell to the goddess through idol immersion on Dashami, before welcoming her again the following year.
Dipankar Chakraborty, a priest at Shahapara Temple in the town, said the goddess arrived this year riding a horse and would depart by boat. According to traditional beliefs, the two modes of transport symbolise social uncertainty and agricultural prosperity, respectively.
Durga Puja is also being celebrated at 445 mandaps across Sunamganj. The five-day festival began on Friday with Maha Shashthi and will conclude on Bijoya Dashami.
The Special Response Battalion (SRB) has stepped up surveillance on social media to prevent rumours and misinformation that could disrupt communal harmony during Durga Puja.
Its cyber team is monitoring Facebook, Instagram and other platforms around the clock, said Wing Commander Tajminur Rahman Chowdhury, commander of SRB-9 Sylhet.
He made the remarks on Friday after inspecting security arrangements at the Durgabari Puja Mandap in Sunamganj town.
He said bomb disposal teams were ready to respond to reports of suspected explosives near puja mandaps. Drone surveillance, special patrols and dog squads have been deployed, while speedboats remain on standby for remote areas. Helicopter support will be provided if necessary.
A strong security cordon has been established across the four districts under SRB-9 to maintain law and order, he added. The force will remain on duty until Bijoya Dashami, the final day of the festival.
